title: French diocesan missals, lane B: Toulouse, Soissons and Vienne originals; scholarly-described states for twelve further dioceses; bounded negatives

uses.finding: Two bounded publication attestations from inspected original leaves: the 1490 Kleblat printing (letter, colophon, calendar) and the 1774 Loménie de Brienne missal (title, pastoral letter, Monitum). These are not a complete sequence, a collated text or a substantive-revision edge.
uses.limit: The 1490 letter exhorts the clergy to use the printed book; the 1772 letter commands the named institutions and priests bound to the Toulouse Office. Neither establishes actual uptake or duration of use. Stage dates are the colophon/title publication years; the 1490 letter shares the colophon date; the 1774 book's letter is dated 29 October 1772.
uses.next_sources: Locate and inspect the 1501–1552 prints and the 1832 missal; resolve 1773 vs 1774; find the dated adoption of the Roman Missal; collate 1490 ferial Gospels, prefaces and sequences against the 1772 letter's account.

uses.finding: Two bounded states: a 1687 Roman Missal with Soissons proper (scholarly description) and the 1745 Fitz-James missal (inspected title and complete letter). Not a complete book, collated text or revision edge.
uses.limit: The letter commands the named institutions and priests bound to the Soissons Office; actual uptake and duration are not established. Its report that churches had used the Roman Missal is a contemporary statement only. Title year 1745 and letter dated 6 January 1745 are both recorded; first use is not dated.
uses.next_sources: Inspect the 1516 and 1531 prints and the post-Tridentine Soissons edition; locate the nineteenth-century Roman adoption act.

uses.finding: Two bounded states: the Lescuyer printing for Vienne use (inspected title, calendar, colophon) and the 1782 promulgation of the provincial missal (described from the pastoral letter by secondary sources). The 1822/1840 provincial missals remain catalogue witnesses.
uses.limit: Title and colophon designate Vienne use for 1519/1520; the 1782 letter addresses the clergy of the whole province with the suffragans' consent. Actual adoption is not established for either. Colophon year 1519 (last day of February); bounds 1519–1520 express year-style uncertainty only. The 1782 stage dates the pastoral letter (approval event); publication 1783 and the catalogue year 1784 are separate events.
uses.next_sources: Inspect the 1784 Missale ad usum provinciae Viennensis and its mandate, the 1822/1840 editions, and the dated adoption of the Roman Missal.

versions.label: 1490 Toulouse missal (Kleblat)
versions.date_label: Printed Toulouse, colophon and prefatory letter both dated 24 July 1490
versions.distinctness_basis: A printed letter in the name of Archbishop Pierre de Lion, the provost Pierre de Rosergio and the chapter says that solemn Masses were celebrated with much discord because manuscript missals were old, faulty or disordered. They therefore had a missal ordered according to the church's rite, corrected by a named canon, and printed by Stephanus Kleblat for distribution throughout the archdiocese, exhorting deans, priors, archpriests and rectors to provide copies and celebrate according to it. The colophon names the book as for the metropolitan church of Saint-Étienne and dates it 24 July 1490. Th
versions.unresolved: No prayer, Ordo or Canon text was read. The letter states a corrective purpose; it does not identify an exemplar or describe specific textual changes. Earlier manuscript Toulouse missals remain uncompared.

versions.label: 1774 Toulouse missal (Loménie de Brienne)
versions.date_label: Title dated 1774; archbishop's pastoral letter dated 29 October 1772 (4 Kal. Nov.)
versions.distinctness_basis: The title names Archbishop Étienne-Charles de Loménie de Brienne's authority with chapter consent. His letter says the new missal was made to agree with his recently published breviary (same Gospels, collects and scriptural chant texts) while keeping the Latin rite and order. It describes the distribution of Gospel and Epistle readings, with at least three ferial Gospels each week (Monday, Wednesday and Friday), each paired with its own Epistle. It says that the old Toulouse missal already gave proper Gospels to Advent ferias except Saturday. Chant texts were largely adopted from French missal
versions.unresolved: The letter's account of change is a contemporary claim; no predecessor missal was collated. The 1772 letter date and the 1774 title date are distinct events. Whether this copy belongs to the same printing as the catalogue's 1773 entry is unresolved.

versions.label: 1687 Roman Missal with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis
versions.date_label: Proper printed at Soissons (Hanisset), cum permissu, 1687 (as described)
versions.distinctness_basis: Leclercq de Laprairie describes a Roman Missal at the church of Acy followed by a 'Proprium Missalis Suessionensis' printed at Soissons by Hanisset with permission in 1687, during a vacancy of the see; the seminary library had another copy. He says the liturgy given by Bishop de Bourlon was that prescribed by Pius V, keeping many local elements. Ledouble confirms that the missal appeared after Bourlon's death, in 1687.
versions.unresolved: Copies described, not viewed; the edition of the Roman Missal is not identified. The 1745 letter's report of churches forced to use the Roman Missal is consistent with this state but is a separate statement.

versions.label: 1745 Soissons missal (Fitz-James)
versions.date_label: Title dated 1745; episcopal letter dated Soissons, 6 January 1745
versions.distinctness_basis: Bishop François de Fitz-James issues the missal after his new breviary. He says that copies of the Soissons missal hardly survived, so almost all churches had been forced to use the Roman Missal, and that Soissons rites survived only orally and were mixed with Roman ones. Apart from the orations, the body of the missal is composed from Scripture. Proper Epistles and Gospels for Wednesdays and Fridays are presented as an old Soissons usage, found in older Soissons missals including one printed shortly after Trent. The Gospels are distributed so that all four evangelists are read in a year. Orat
versions.unresolved: The letter's comparison with earlier practice is a contemporary claim; no earlier Soissons missal or Roman Missal was collated. The post-Tridentine Soissons edition it mentions is unidentified.

versions.label: 1519/1520 Vienne missal (Lescuyer, Lyon)
versions.date_label: Colophon: printed at Lyon, last day of February 1519 (possibly 1520 new style)
versions.distinctness_basis: The colophon calls it the missal for the use of the holy church of Vienne, with very many offices newly added, printed at Lyon by Bernard Lescuyer on the last day of February 1519. The February calendar lists the Vienne bishops Avitus (5 February) and Simplicius (11 February), and Paschasius (22 February), with folio references to the sanctoral.
versions.unresolved: The phrase 'offices newly added' names no specific Masses, and no earlier Vienne missal was compared. No bishop's mandate was seen. The date bounds cover the year-style uncertainty, not a duration.

versions.label: 1782 Vienne provincial missal (Lefranc de Pompignan)
versions.date_label: Pastoral letter dated 18 August 1782 promulgating the missal and breviary; publication reported as 1783; catalogue year 1784
versions.distinctness_basis: The 1849 survey describes Archbishop Lefranc de Pompignan's pastoral letter of 18 August 1782. It is addressed to the clergy of Vienne and, with the comprovincial bishops' consent, to the clergy of each diocese of the province, and it promulgates the new missal and breviary together. The author says Pompignan replaced the earlier Villars liturgy by adopting the Paris books of Vintimille, Viger and Mésenguy with some cuts, additions and corrections, after the provincial assembly of 1775. Pompignan's 1903 biographer notes that the breviary and missal were published in 1783 at Grenoble by the wid
versions.unresolved: The letter was not viewed; its content is reported by a polemical survey. Publication is reported as 1783, while the catalogue witness is dated 1784; edition identity with the witness is assumed, not verified. The extent of dependence on the Paris missal is the author's judgement, not a collation.

versions.label: 1520 Nantes missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
versions.date_label: 1520 printing, as described by Duine from BnF Rés. B.1814
versions.distinctness_basis: Duine describes the BnF copy as a quarto printed at Rouen by Martin Morin. At fol. CIII, after the ordinary Gloria, it has the Marian-farced 'Gloria de beata Maria', which Duine notes is not peculiar to Breton use.
versions.unresolved: Scholarly description only; the original was not viewed. Copy identity with the USUARIUM 1520 record is assumed at edition level, not verified.

versions.label: 1588 Nantes missal (Philippe du Bec)
versions.date_label: 1588 printing at Nantes (Vincent Hucet), title transcribed by Duine
versions.distinctness_basis: Duine transcribes the title of the Nantes municipal library copy. It was issued by mandate of Bishop Philippe du Bec, as approaching nearest to the Tridentine exemplar ('Ad exemplar Tridentinum proxime accedens'), and recently emended by men delegated in the Nantes synod. It was printed at Nantes by Vincent Hucet with royal privilege in 1588: a folio in roman type, in two columns.
versions.unresolved: The title's claim of approximation to the Tridentine missal is the book's self-description reported by Duine; the extent of conformity to the 1570 Roman Missal is not collated. Duine's section heading prints the year ambiguously; the transcribed title ends 1588.

versions.label: 1492 Rennes missal (Michel Guibé)
versions.date_label: Colophon: finished at Paris, 10 January 1492 (as quoted by Duine); year style not stated, so possibly January 1493 by modern reckoning
versions.distinctness_basis: Duine quotes the colophon. The missal and ordinary of the Mass, with the church's constitutions and customs added, omissions supplied and errors emended, was prepared by order of Bishop Michel Guibé through four named clergy and printed at Paris at the cost of the booksellers André Hodian and Jean Alexandre. It was finished on 10 January 1492.
versions.unresolved: Duine does not say whether the January date follows a year beginning at Easter; the bounds 1492–1493 express that year-style uncertainty, not a duration. Original not viewed; the described BnF copy is the holding of catalogue witness 7428, whose own age field is malformed.

versions.label: 1523 Rennes missal (Yves Mahyeuc)
versions.date_label: 1523 printing at Paris (Jean de Kerbriant), as described by Duine
versions.distinctness_basis: Duine quotes the title, which mentions the church's institutions and customs. He reports from the last page that the missal was corrected by order of Bishop Yves Mahyeuc and approved by him. It gained Masses of Our Lady of Pity, St Roch, St Claude and the Holy Name, and was printed at Paris by Jean de Kerbriant, alias Huguelin, in 1523.
versions.unresolved: Duine paraphrases the final page; the added Masses are reported, not collated against 1492. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1531 Rennes missal (Caen)
versions.date_label: Title imprint 1531, printed at Caen (as described by Duine)
versions.distinctness_basis: The title, as transcribed, says the missal was skilfully emended with several additions and newly joined Masses; Duine lists the Holy Name, Lacryma Christi, Visitation, Roch, Genevieve and Martha. He notes farced Kyries and two Glorias. He also notes that the Mass ends with the Placeat, without a final blessing or last Gospel.
versions.unresolved: No bishop is named. Duine's remark that the Mass ends at the Placeat is his observation of one copy. The 1533 entry may be a second issue of this edition (Duine against Delisle).

versions.label: 1588 Rennes missal (Aymar Hennequin)
versions.date_label: 1588 printing at Rennes (Pierre Bretel), title transcribed by Duine
versions.distinctness_basis: Duine transcribes the title of the Grand Séminaire copy. It was restored and emended by order of Bishop Aymar Hennequin with the chapter's consent, and printed at Rennes by Pierre Bretel in 1588 with royal privilege. The sequences are gathered at the end, to be said or omitted at the celebrant's choice. The Ordinarium Missae offers an alternative litany-form Kyrie in three forms (fol. 159v–160r).
versions.unresolved: Original not viewed; not among the Amiet-table witnesses. No claim of Roman conformity is made by the transcribed title.

versions.label: 1535 Vannes missal (Paris, Yolande Bonhomme)
versions.date_label: 1535 printing, as reported by Duine
versions.distinctness_basis: Duine reports a copy in the Vannes episcopal library, printed at Paris by Yolande Bonhomme, widow of Thielman Kerver, for Nantes and Vannes booksellers. An old manuscript note in the 1589 breviary, which he quotes, says that this missal gave St Denis a sequence and Credo for the whole diocese.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: Duine gives no title, colophon or mandate text, and the contents claim is second-hand through a manuscript note. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1526 Léon missal (Paris, Nicolas Prévost)
versions.date_label: 1526 printing at Paris, per the last leaf as reported by Duine
versions.distinctness_basis: Duine reports from the last leaf that the missal was printed in 1526 at Paris by Nicolas Prévost at the cost of Yves Quilleveré. He quotes the phrase 'prefateque ecclesie ritui adaptatum', which he interprets as adapting the Léon liturgy to the Paris liturgy. He notes a Confiteor that does not copy the Roman formula, two different Glorias and farced Kyries.
versions.unresolved: The quoted Latin phrase literally refers to the rite of 'the aforesaid church'; Duine's reading of it as Paris use is his interpretation and is not adopted here. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1742 Sées missal (Néel de Christot)
versions.date_label: Missal printed 1742 (Hommey); mandate date not given
versions.distinctness_basis: Hommey says Bishop Néel de Christot completed Jacques Lallemant's liturgy and promulgated its missal and ritual. He adds that the missal, printed in 1742, and Néel de Christot's 1745 breviary did not agree with Lallemant's breviary. Marais and Beaudouin date Lallemant's breviary mandement to 15 August 1737 and say that the Roman breviary had been in use at Sées for over a century before it.
versions.unresolved: No original page or mandate text was viewed; the content of the missal is not described beyond its relation to the breviaries.

versions.label: 1516 Thérouanne missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
versions.date_label: Final note: 12 November 1516 (as reported in French by the bibliography)
versions.distinctness_basis: The bibliography transcribes the title and a final note. The missal was printed at the cost of Jean and Antoine Lagache, booksellers at Arras, on 12 November 1516, by Martin Morin at Rouen.
versions.unresolved: Publication facts only; no contents described. Component scope is nominal. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1518 Thérouanne missal (Paris, Nicolas de Pratis)
versions.date_label: Colophon: Paris, 11 September 1518 (as transcribed)
versions.distinctness_basis: The transcribed title calls the missal well ordered and carefully corrected, with the sequences set in their places and several Masses added that had never before been printed in that use. The colophon reads Paris, Nicolas de Pratis, at the expense of de Pratis and Jean de Laporte, 11 September 1518. A calendar with monthly health advice follows.
versions.unresolved: The added Masses are not named; no collation with 1516. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1497 Troyes missal (Paris, Jean du Pré)
versions.date_label: Colophon dated 17 February 1497 at Paris (as described by Lalore); year style not stated, so possibly February 1498 by modern reckoning
versions.distinctness_basis: Lalore describes the 1497 missal printed at Paris by Jean du Pré for the Troyes bookseller Nicolas Ludot, with a colophon calling the book corrected of errors.
versions.unresolved: Publication facts only; component scope nominal. Lalore also lists an earlier 1492 edition, not among the Amiet-table witnesses. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1525 Troyes missal (Le Coq)
versions.date_label: Colophon dated 1525 (as described by Lalore)
versions.distinctness_basis: Lalore quotes the colophon of the 1525 Le Coq printing, which reports added Masses of SS Joseph, Godo and Edmund.
versions.unresolved: Added Masses reported, not collated against 1497. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1580 Troyes missal (Claude de Bauffremont)
versions.date_label: Bishop's mandate dated 1 March 1580; printed 1580
versions.distinctness_basis: Lalore describes the 1580 edition, whose title says it was recently emended by the bishop's mandate. He prints Bishop Claude de Bauffremont's Latin mandate for it, dated at Troyes on 1 March 1580. Lalore reports that the 1615 Troyes missal is a reprint of this edition.
versions.unresolved: The mandate does not claim conformity to the 1570 Roman Missal; no collation. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1696 Roman Missal with Troyes supplement
versions.date_label: Supplement printed 1696; use described in the 1736 mandate
versions.distinctness_basis: Bossuet's 1736 mandate says that Troyes missals had become so scarce that all churches, including the cathedral, had long used only 'foreign missals', which his predecessors had tolerated. Lalore's footnote identifies these as the Roman Missal with the diocesan supplement printed in 1696 under the title Orationes addendae Missali Romano … ritu dioecesis Trecensis (Troyes, Charles Briden).
versions.unresolved: The duration and universality of this use are the 1736 mandate's statement; the supplement's contents are not described beyond its title. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1736 Troyes missal (Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet)
versions.date_label: First mandate 16 September 1735; publication mandate 26 September 1736
versions.distinctness_basis: Lalore prints Bishop Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet's Latin mandate of 16 September 1735 and his French mandate of 26 September 1736. The latter presents the missal as made to answer the new breviary, prepared by learned men chosen with the chapter, and as the awaited replacement for the foreign missals whose use his predecessors had tolerated; Lalore's chronology (p. 111) records it as making the new missal obligatory. Lalore's chronology records a royal commission under Cardinal de Rohan, a Conseil d'État arrêt of 11 June 1737, and Bossuet's fourth pastoral instruction and ordinance of 15 October 1738, in which he retracted several provisions of the missal and restored the former rubrics on three principal points (pp. 112, 117).
versions.unresolved: The ordered corrections of 1738 imply a corrected state whose printed form was not seen; no collation with the Roman Missal or the 1580 book. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1532 Mâcon missal (Lyon, Denys de Harsy)
versions.date_label: Colophon dated 15 March 1532 (as described)
versions.distinctness_basis: The Notes describe a 1532 Mâcon missal printed at Lyon by Denys de Harsy, with a colophon of 15 March 1532. Its title says it was newly emended and carefully corrected, with several new offices not seen before. The book bears the arms of Bishop Hémard de Denonville and contains Temporale, Sanctorale and Commune.
versions.unresolved: New offices are claimed but not named; no collation. Original not viewed; not among the Amiet-table witnesses.

versions.label: 1509 Verdun missal (Paris, Wolfgang Hopyl)
versions.date_label: 1509 printing (as described)
versions.distinctness_basis: The Petite bibliothèque verdunoise describes the 1509 missal printed on vellum at Paris by Wolfgang Hopyl by order of the chapter while the see was vacant: 284 leaves, the Verdun copy perhaps unique. The Pouillé also records it.
versions.unresolved: Publication facts only; no contents. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1554 Verdun missal (Nicolas Psaulme)
versions.date_label: Title year 1554; the Pouillé dates a reprint to 1557
versions.distinctness_basis: The Petite bibliothèque verdunoise transcribes the title: newly and carefully revised by Bishop Nicolas Psaulme, with many additions never printed before, including several Mass offices, and printed at the bishop's expense in 1554. It describes the divisions: preliminaries, Proper of Time with the Ordo Missae up to the Canon, Canon, Sanctorale, Common and votives. The Pouillé instead says that Psaulme had the Verdun missal reprinted in 1557.
versions.unresolved: The 1554/1557 discrepancy is unresolved and may reflect two issues. The revision is pre-Tridentine and makes no Roman-conformity claim. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1556 Meaux missal (Louis de Brézé)
versions.date_label: 1556 edition (Allou)
versions.distinctness_basis: Allou says that in 1556 Bishop Louis de Brézé gave a new edition of Jean L'Huillier's missal, corrected by his care. Allou dates L'Huillier's printed missal to 1492.
versions.unresolved: Corrections not specified; original not viewed.

versions.label: 1709 Meaux missal (Henri de Thiard de Bissy)
versions.date_label: Published 1709 (Allou)
versions.distinctness_basis: Allou says that Bishop Henri de Thiard de Bissy reprinted all the Meaux liturgical books. The missal, already worked on in Bossuet's time, appeared in 1709. The 1713 breviary followed, with many changes and a psalter distribution different from the Roman.
versions.unresolved: Allou's explicit non-Roman remark concerns the 1713 breviary; the missal's contents are not described. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1836 Meaux missal (Pruneau, under Gallard)
versions.date_label: Missal appeared 1836 (Allou); breviary 1834
versions.distinctness_basis: Allou says that because the Meaux books were running out, the Paris breviary and missal were adopted provisionally for the cathedral in 1824. Bishop Gallard then gave the diocese a new liturgy, with breviary offices following Paris and the rest by Canon Pruneau. The breviary appeared in 1834 and Pruneau's missal in 1836. The 1849 survey confirms the 1834 Pruneau liturgy and lists Meaux as having its own liturgy.
versions.unresolved: Contents not described; the 1845 reissue was not found. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1642 Meaux missal (Dominique Séguier)
versions.date_label: Missal dated 1642 (Allou)
versions.distinctness_basis: Allou says that Séguier printed several liturgical books, that his 1640 breviary preface announced harmonising the Meaux liturgy with that of the universal Church, and that the missal is dated 1642. A catalogue record gives the missal's title as 'ad formam sacrosancti concilii Tridentini restitutum'.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: applying the breviary's stated Roman harmonisation to the missal is an inference supported only by a catalogue title. Original not viewed.

versions.label: Noyon missal of Charles de Broglie (attested by 1774)
versions.date_label: Attested by derivative books of 1774 and 1777; no printing year given
versions.distinctness_basis: The Bibliographie noyonnaise records the title of a Missale Noviomense issued by Bishop Charles de Broglie's authority with chapter consent, known through a 1780 chapter memoir. It lists a 1774 Eucologe and 1777 Heures for Noyon that follow Bourzac's breviary and 'the missal printed by order of Mgr de Broglie'.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: no copy, printing year or contents described. The Amiet-table year 1770 is not confirmed here.

versions.label: 1785 Sisteron missal (Suffren; Toulouse liturgy)
versions.date_label: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785 (cited imprint)
versions.distinctness_basis: Albanès says Bishop Suffren introduced a new liturgy that had nothing of Sisteron but the name, being the Toulouse liturgy, even down to a proper preface for St Saturninus. Everything was printed at Toulouse: the breviary in 1778 and the missal seven years later, in 1785. His footnote cites the imprint: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785, quarto.
versions.unresolved: The identification with the Toulouse liturgy is the historian's, citing contemporary opinion; no collation with the 1774 Toulouse missal. Original not viewed.

versions.label: 1779 Montauban breviary-and-missal mandement
versions.date_label: Mandement dated 24 February 1779; obligatory from 28 November 1779 (Daux)
versions.distinctness_basis: Daux reports a mandement of 24 February 1779 ordering in all churches the new breviary and missal of Montauban, with gradual and vesperal. The bishop says he chose, for uniformity with the metropolis, the breviary and missal already adopted by the other Toulouse suffragans, and their use became obligatory from 28 November 1779. Daux says the diocese was the last in France to take it.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: no printed missal is identified. The catalogue's 1773 Missale Montalbanense and 1774 Missae pro defunctis predate this mandement, and the 1772 Nouvelles ecclésiastiques (cited in the 1849 survey) already lists Montauban among sees taking a Paris-type breviary. The conflict is unresolved.

versions.label: Rieux adoption of the Paris missal (reported 1778)
versions.date_label: Reported in the Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 as done 'some time ago'
versions.distinctness_basis: The Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 report that Bishop de Lastic of Rieux had some time earlier wished to adopt the Paris breviary and missal in place of the Roman books still in use in the diocese. The chapter consented and left him the choice of edition. He chose the latest, which included the office and Mass of the Sacred Heart, to the displeasure of the chapter and many parish priests.
versions.unresolved: Provisional: a partisan periodical report; no Rieux missal is described. The catalogue's 1776 Missale Rivense may be the resulting book, but that link is not stated by the source.

versions.label: 1827 Nîmes diocesan liturgy (Larèche)
versions.date_label: Change dated 1827 by the 1849 survey
versions.distinctness_basis: The 1849 survey says that in 1827 Nîmes left the Roman for an entirely new liturgy composed by the abbé Larèche, vicar general of Bishop de Chaffoy; its table lists Nîmes as having its own liturgy. L'épiscopat français records that the diocesan synod of 27–29 September 1851 decreed the replacement of the Nîmes liturgy by the Roman.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Selected stages: french-dioceses-b-batch4:toulouse-1490, french-dioceses-b-batch4:toulouse-1774
gap_dispositions.remaining: Documented: 1490 (Kleblat; letter and colophon 24 July 1490) and 1774 (Loménie de Brienne; letter 29 October 1772). Missing: 1501–1552 prints, identity of the 'old Toulouse missal' the 1772 letter cites, 1773/1774 issue question, 1832 missal, Roman-Missal adoption date, and any text collation.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Selected stages: french-dioceses-b-batch4:soissons-1687, french-dioceses-b-batch4:soissons-1745
gap_dispositions.remaining: Documented: 1687 Roman Missal with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis (description); 1745 Fitz-James (original; letter 6 January 1745). Missing: 1516 and 1531 prints, the post-Tridentine Soissons missal, post-1745 printings and the 1852 Roman restoration mandement (effective Advent 1852 per Ledouble).

gap_dispositions.evidence: Selected stages: french-dioceses-b-batch4:vienne-1519, french-dioceses-b-batch4:vienne-1782
gap_dispositions.remaining: Documented: Lyon 1519/1520 (Lescuyer; original) and the 1782 provincial missal promulgation (Lefranc de Pompignan; described). Missing: intervening editions, an inspected copy of the provincial missal (published 1783 per biographer; catalogue 1784), the 1820/1822/1840 reprints, and the Roman restorations in the successor sees.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Batch 4 lane B inspected the Halberstadt mandate leaf (Google Books xhKLX-OS2c0C PP7) on 2026-10-21. Google Books full-view searches found no Lübeck or Merseburg missal ('missale lubicense', 'missale lubecense', 'missale merseburgense'). This index row keeps its catalogue character; no book sequence is constructed.
gap_dispositions.remaining: Single catalogue witnesses only. Inspect holding catalogues, exact titles, colophons, contents, rights and complete extents; resolve the Lübeck USTC references. No continuous local-use chronology, normative revision, original-book completeness or modern survival is established.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Batch 4 lane B queried the BnF catalogue SRU (bib.title) on 2026-10-21 for Missale Rupellense, Alesiense, Aturense, Blesense, Electense, 'Royensis propriorum', 'ecclesiae Sosmensis' and Nanceiense. Five records give diocesan identity through the bishop or place named (La Rochelle 1835, Aire 1844, Blois 1741, Alet 1774, Nancy-Toul 1838); Alesiense, Royensis and Sosmensis returned no record. This index row keeps no book sequence.
gap_dispositions.remaining: Resolve exact use, physical-copy and edition identities from original imprints and holding-library records; inspect contents, rights and reception before any recension, Catholic affiliation or geographical mapping. Repeated catalogue rows in a cluster are not independent edition counts.

gap_dispositions.remaining: Documented (scholarly description): 1520 Rouen print; 1588 du Bec missal. Missing: inspected originals, 1482 and lost 1501 editions, the c.1780 Poitiers-type liturgy, the 1837 missal, the 1858 Roman adoption act.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Selected stages: french-dioceses-b-batch4:rennes-1492, french-dioceses-b-batch4:rennes-1523, french-dioceses-b-batch4:rennes-1531, french-dioceses-b-batch4:rennes-1588
gap_dispositions.remaining: Documented (scholarly description): 1492, 1523, 1531, 1588. Missing: originals, c.1485/1500/1533/1557 entries, 1776/1786/1830/1831 missals, the 1780 cathedral-only Tours liturgy, and the Roman adoption act (1846 vs 1848 in sources).

gap_dispositions.evidence: ; provisional: french-dioceses-b-batch4:vannes-1535

remaining_gaps: french-dioceses-b-batch4:toulouse-sequence-gap: Original 1501, 1524, 1539, 1540 and 1552 prints; the 'old Toulouse missal' the 1772 letter compares, and its identity relative to the 1490 book; component collation of ferial Gospels, prefaces and sequences across the two states.

french-dioceses-b-batch4:toulouse-19th-century: The 1773 catalogue entry (identity with 1774), the 1832 Missale Tolosanum, and the dated act for the adoption of the Roman Missal. L'épiscopat français (1907, p. 626) says Archbishop Mioland prepared, and Archbishop Desprez carried out from 1861, the re-establishment of the Roman liturgy; the 1849 survey lists Toulouse as Parisian.

french-dioceses-b-batch4:soissons-before-1745: Original 1516 and 1531 prints; the Soissons missal 'printed shortly after Trent' named in the 1745 letter; dated evidence of the de facto use of the Roman Missal that the letter reports.

french-dioceses-b-batch4:soissons-after-1745: Inspected later printings, and the Roman restoration act. Ledouble (1880, pp. 383–385, 120) states that the Fitz-James liturgy stayed in use until 1852, that the provincial council of October 1849 decided the return, that the diocesan Proper was approved on 18 July 1851, and that the Roman liturgy was resumed from the first Sunday of Advent 1852 under Bishop de Garsignies. Leclercq de Laprairie (1852, p. 18) says Garsignies had just prescribed it.

french-dioceses-b-batch4:vienne-later-sequence: Intervening sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Vienne missals, including the 1676 Villars liturgy the 1849 survey names; an inspected copy of the 1782/1783/1784 provincial missal; the 1822/1840 reprints (the 1849 survey saw a Grenoble 1820 provincial edition); and, after 1801, the Roman restorations in the successor sees (L'épiscopat français p. 263: Grenoble 1869).

french-dioceses-b-batch4:nantes-gaps: Inspected originals of the 1482, 1520 and 1588 missals; Duine's lost 1501 Larchier edition; the eighteenth-century change (the 1849 survey says Nantes preferred the Poitiers liturgy of the Lazarist Jacob at the 1780 Tours provincial assembly, and its table lists Nantes as 'de Poitiers'); the 1837 Missale Nannetense; and the Roman adoption, dated 1858 in a Duine footnote without a mandate date.

french-dioceses-b-batch4:rennes-gaps: Inspected originals; the undated c.1485 print and the 1500, 1533 and 1557 entries; the 1776/1786 Missale Redonense and 1830/1831 Rhedonense; the 1849 survey's statement that in 1780 the bishop took the Tours liturgy for the cathedral only and kept the Roman liturgy obligatory elsewhere; and the Roman adoption, 1846 (1849 survey p. 381) against 1848 (Duine p. 7 footnote).

french-dioceses-b-batch4:vannes-gaps: Inspected originals of the 1530 (Regnault) and 1535 missals; any later Vannes missal; the 1849 survey's statement that Vannes kept its Paris books in 1780; and the Roman adoption, 1847 (1849 survey p. 381) against 1848 (Duine p. 7).

limits: Gallica, the main host of digitised French diocesan missals, refused automated access (Cloudflare 403) throughout, and archive.org/BVMM were unreachable; most routes therefore rest on exact-locus nineteenth-century scholarship rather than inspected originals. Originals were inspected only for Toulouse 1490 (Rosalis), Toulouse 1774 and Soissons 1745 (Google Books), Vienne 1519/1520 (Numelyo, web resolution) and the Halberstadt mandate leaf. Three helper sub-agents read scholarship page images; the owner re-viewed the key loci listed in the worklog. No transition is asserted: letters and scholars describe changes relative to earlier practice, but no predecessor text was collated. Provisional-only routes keep the no-new-researched-stage-sequence status. Dates of Roman-Missal adoption are recorded in gaps with their conflicts (Rennes 1846/1848, Vannes 1847/1848, Troyes 1846/1847, Montauban 1779 vs catalogue 1773).

independent_review.scope: All 34 added stages (28 documented, 6 provisional) were checked against page images of their cited loci: the Toulouse 1490 Rosalis leaves were refetched; Duine, Du Lac, Hommey, Marais-Beaudouin, Albanès, Allou, Ledouble, the Saint-Omer bibliography and the Mende history were re-read in independent archive.org copies; and the Google-hosted sources, Toulouse 1774, Soissons 1745 and Vienne 1519/1520 were read on lane-acquired images whose SHA-256 matched the lane fetch logs, because Google Books answered with its CAPTCHA redirect and Numelyo with HTTP 502. All 12 new candidates were checked for identity against the whole Western inventory. Three duplicated existing witnesses (Rennes 7428, Soissons 7113, Halberstadt 5818) and were removed; their evidence now qualifies those records. The audit and TOML were diffed semantically against 5f2e74718. Corrections narrowed wording, witness identity, date bounds and one source kind, and restored a dropped Rennes decision. No new research claims, stages, transitions or candidates were added. Not checked: fresh Google or Numelyo fetches, the Toulouse Monitum page, and gap rows whose sources are cited only as text.
